mechanism: Williams fractal (2n+1 centered window) is confirmed only after n trailing bars close; features publish at confirmation bar t (center t-n), not at the extremum bar. One closed-window pass yields fractal high/low flags, strength = extremum/window-mean - 1 (or mirrored for lows), validity via fixed floor or dynamic floor = threshold * volatility[center], S/R as max/min of last lookback confirmed fractal events (event-count ring, not bar count), distances of bar midpoint to those levels, breakouts when close clears the center-bar high/low paired with opposite fractal, and a trend block: breakout density and signed balance over ma_period that gate buy/sell with signal_strength = fractal_strength / volatility.
data_needed: OHLC bars plus a volatility series (e.g. ATR as fraction of price) for dynamic threshold and signal sizing; stateful rings of confirmed extremes and recent breakout flags.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic 1,200 hourly bars with variance-clustering; generic MT5 symbol/period via iCustom; broker-discrete prices noted.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a leak-safe structural swing sensor suite: event-based S/R levels, continuous distance features, and breakout-density regime/trend gates with volatility-scaled strength — not a chart marker port.
quote: Every value it returns for bar t refers to the fractal centered at t-n, which makes the Python contract explicit rather than implicit

mechanism: For each bar, fit OLS of (log) price vs local time over every candidate horizon L in span; keep slope, R², and t-value of the window with largest |t|. Feature mode forces lookforward=False so the window ends at the current bar (reverse series, fit, reverse results). Optional volatility_threshold zero-masks windows whose local std falls below an expanding quantile. Wrapper drops label-only columns (t1, ret, bin) so only window/slope/t_value/rsquared enter X.
data_needed: Close (or signed series with use_log=False); candidate span (e.g. 5–20); optional local volatility series for masking.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: 3,000-bar synthetic random walks; 500-bar synthetic with three injected drift regimes (hourly framing); method aimed at general price series including intraday.
why_new_for_mis: Adaptive-horizon trend confidence sensor: per-bar chosen L, slope, and t-value that distinguish sharp short moves from shallow long drifts without a fixed MA period — causal for live MIS features.
quote: A sharp two-bar move and a shallow twelve-bar drift can both register as a strong trend, at different L, without either being diluted by forcing one window length on both.

mechanism: argmax|t| across unequal L compares Student-t stats on different df and systematically favors short windows (worked example: L=5 selected though L=20 is ~286× more significant and opposite sign). Correction: convert each candidate to two-sided p-value (or signed-z via InvNorm) before selecting. Separately, OLS trend on I(1) prices inflates t (95th pct of max |t| ≈ 21 under driftless RW vs nominal ~2.0); calibrate critical values by simulating the same scan under a trendless random-walk null of length max(L).
data_needed: Same trend-scanning outputs plus df=L-2; offline/on-init Monte Carlo of driftless RW under the configured span.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Deterministic y=100+0.05i+3sin(0.3i); 20k driftless RW of 260 obs, L∈[5,40]; applies to price-level series generally.
why_new_for_mis: Turns raw trend-scan t into a comparable, null-calibrated regime-significance score instead of a spuriously always-significant feature — critical before MIS thresholds on trend evidence.
quote: Applying the nominal threshold to these trendless series flags 99.94 percent of bars as significantly trending.

mechanism: MQL5 CTrendScanningFeatures keeps per-horizon running sums (sum_y, sum_y2, sum_ty) updated O(1) when the window slides; seeds O(L) once. Independent causal fit exposed that Python lookforward=False reversed time without negating slope/t — corrected by negating both. Optional TrendScanSignificance maps t to signed-z via Lanczos log-gamma / incomplete beta for length-fair horizon pick and RW-calibrated crit95 gating in EAs. Default volatility_threshold=0.0 collapses to expanding min std mask.
data_needed: Close series; horizon list from BuildHorizons(min,max); optional use_log; calibrated threshold cache.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Parity on synthetic closes; EA read via iCustom on _Symbol/_Period; span(5,20) used throughout series.
why_new_for_mis: Deployable online trend-horizon sensor with correct chronological sign and length-corrected significance — ready for MIS live buffers, not just Python research.
quote: A positive t_value now means what it should: the fitted trend, using only bars up to and including the current one, is rising.

series_key: from static ma to adaptive filtering
mechanism: Self-Adaptive Moving Average is an NLMS adaptive FIR: predict = w·x_past, error = price - predict, then w ← w + (μ/E)·e·x with E = Σx². Optional Kaufman Efficiency Ratio scales μ_eff = μ·(0.5+ER) so learning accelerates in directional regimes and damps in chop. ATR clamps |error| before the update to survive news spikes; leakage γ decays weights; optional Σw=1 keeps output on price scale. Train on price, first differences, or returns (reconstructed to price). Slope of SAMA line colors up/down/flat as a visual regime tag. Weights update only on closed bars.
data_needed: OHLC (or close/typical), ATR for clamp, ER window of net direction vs path length; persistent weight vector.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Design for live MT5 charts/EAs/backtests; Part 2 shows EURUSD H1; multi-TF hierarchy (H4/H1/M15) proposed as extension; FX and high-priced instruments discussed.
why_new_for_mis: Regime-aware adaptive smoother whose learning rate itself is a market-state sensor (ER) and whose residual/ATR clamp is a spike-robustness sensor — replaces static MA period retuning.
quote: During a sustained trend, the ER approaches 1.0 and the effective learning rate rises toward 1.5× the base value, allowing the filter to track price tightly. During consolidation, the ER collapses and the learning rate is suppressed toward 0.5× base

series_key: from static ma to adaptive filtering
mechanism: Production SAMA_NLMS.mq5 exposes the adaptive line for regime classification: price above SAMA → allow longs only; below → shorts. Filter tightens in fast trends and flattens in ranges because weights adapt online; path dependence mitigated by warmup_bars (default 500) silent training. Can pair with fixed SMA for crossover change signals. INPUT_RET recommended on thin/illiquid sessions to avoid over-adaptation to noise.
data_needed: Closed-bar SAMA buffer (shift 1), close; same NLMS inputs as Part 1.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 chart demo; practical starting profile for most FX symbols; timeframe switch rebuilds weights from zero.
why_new_for_mis: Concrete online adaptive-mean regime gate with documented closed-bar training and history-depth caveats — usable as an MIS regime channel alongside static MAs.
quote: Because the filter adapts dynamically, it tightens automatically during fast trends. It also flattens during messy ranges. This behavior eliminates false regime flips compared to traditional, fixed-period averages.

mechanism: Per new closed bar, take WindowLength closes as y, standardize, fit GP (RBF + GaussianLikelihood + ExactInference) with X = time indices 1..W, predict one step ahead at X*=W+1, destandardize mean and variance, plot predictive mean and ±z·σ bands. Retrain/reset hyperparameters each bar on a sliding window — online Bayesian sensor of level and predictive uncertainty.
data_needed: Close prices; window length; z-score for bands; optional RMSE vs naive benchmark.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD minute-TF RMSE example cited; general symbol/period; synthetic sin+linear regression tests.
why_new_for_mis: Uncertainty-aware one-step price sensor: predictive variance bands are a live volatility/confidence channel, not just a point forecast.
quote: By using a sliding window to form the training sample and continuously retraining the model, it implements the principle of adaptation to changing market conditions.

mechanism: Sliding window builds X from NumLags prior close increments and y ∈ {+1,−1} from next-bar close direction; normalize features; fit GP with RBF + LogitLikelihood + LaplaceInference; predict P(up) and class for the current bar from the latest lag vector. Arrows fire only if class probability clears ProbabilityThreshold. Optional accuracy vs naive same-direction benchmark.
data_needed: Close series; WindowLength, NumLags, ProbabilityThreshold; online Fit each new bar.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart-attached indicator on any symbol/period; XOR synthetic classification validation at 98% accuracy.
why_new_for_mis: Bayesian sequence/lag classifier emitting calibrated direction probabilities for MIS change sensing, with explicit probability gating rather than hard labels only.
quote: The features used are increments of closing prices, which are calculated in a sliding window of historical data.

mechanism: Hidden bullish: RSI lower-low after bearish-then-3-bullish RSI pattern while price makes higher low, with price and current close above 200 EMA; hidden bearish: RSI higher-high after bullish-then-3-bearish pattern while price lower high, below 200 EMA. Stochastic %K must cross back through oversold(20)/overbought(80) within 11 bars of the new RSI extreme before entry; SL at last swing low/high.
data_needed: iMA(200 EMA), iRSI(14), iStochastic(5,3,3); OHLC over ~30 bars; swing high/low from candle color flips.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol with PERIOD_CURRENT (chart TF); educational EA, no fixed symbol named.
why_new_for_mis: Continuation-style hidden-divergence sensor (momentum vs price structure) gated by EMA regime and timed Stochastic confirmation — a concrete multi-indicator change detector for MIS.
quote: At this point, the RSI forms a lower low (LL) while the price forms a higher low (HL). This divergence implies that the RSI is weak, suggesting possible upward momentum in the future, even though the matching price (C-Price) made a higher bottom.

mechanism: Beginner file-handling project: read Trading_Journal.csv Profit($) column, cumulative-sum into a balance curve, plot axes/labels in a separate indicator window via OnInit/OnTimer. No market regime, volatility, liquidity, or price-sequence sensing is built.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Account trade journal only; not market data.
why_new_for_mis: After full read: language/UI tutorial for account P/L visualization — out of MIS market-sensing scope.
quote: This project's objective is to use trade data from a CSV file to visualize a balance curve.
